Swimlane.doc: Who does what, and where work waits.

props.name: lanes
props.type: { owner: string; steps: { name: string; waiting?: boolean | undefined; }[]; }[]

Trail.doc: One request traced stop by stop. The total wait is computed here, never taken from the model.

props.name: stops
props.type: { owner: string; name: string; note: string; waitDays: number; }[]

Bottlenecks.doc: Where work waits most, as ranked bars.

Priority.doc: Sorts items by impact and effort. The caption is fixed text: this is a judgement, not a measurement.

Funnel.doc: How many make it through each step. The share kept at each step is computed here.

Compare.doc: Today against a mapped version, row by row.

props.name: rows
props.type: { label: string; left: string; right: string; }[]

GuaranteeCard.doc: One guarantee: statement, check, deadline, remedy and status.

VerifyStatus.doc: Shows what the verifier found. It renders only a VerifyResult from verifyRecord (as a prop or from RecordProvider). With no result it says "Not verified" and never a pass.

LedgerTimeline.doc: The hash-chained ledger. Events come from the verifier, so a broken link or bad signature shows in red.

RetestClock.doc: A deadline against a clock. Pass `now` for a fixed reading (tests, server render), or `live` to tick. Outcome words come from the dates, not from the caller.

ConfidenceBar.doc: An observed pass rate with its exact interval. The interval and the verdict are computed here from passes and n alone. A small n gives a wide band, which is the point: 50 cases never prove 90%.

ApprovalGate.doc: A human approval step. Escalation counts as a correct outcome, not a failure.

RecordProvider.doc: Hands a verifier result (and optionally the manifest) to the record components below it. The OpenUI versions of VerifyStatus, LedgerTimeline and GuaranteeCard read from here and cannot be given a result, so a model can place them but cannot write what they say.

EvalMatrix.doc: Cases by runs, with the pass rate and exact interval per run and a paired comparison of any two runs.

FleetBoard.doc: One row per deployment, with the tightest deadline computed from its clocks. Sort and filter in place.

props.name: rows
props.type: { name: string; status: "breached" | "ok" | "watch"; clocks: { label: string; startedAt: string; deadlineHours: number; }[]; model?: string | undefined; }[]

ChainGraph.doc: The ledger as linked blocks. A broken link or a bad signature shows where the chain stops being trustworthy.

ReceiptCard.doc: A signed receipt for one action. Signature validity comes from your verifier, passed in as `signers`.

TraceExplorer.doc: A trace you can actually read: flame graph, waterfall and ranked list over one time axis, with a draggable minimap, zoom, search, critical path, a legend that shows each kind's share of time, and a detail panel. Every figure (self time, share, totals, critical path) is computed from the spans.

JsonTree.doc: A collapsible view of any JSON-like value: typed colours, click a key to copy its path, long strings fold, big arrays show the first 100 entries, and circular references are cut instead of looped on.

DiffViewer.doc: A review-grade diff for policies, prompts and outputs: file list with change counts, hunk headers, old and new line numbers, unchanged stretches folded until you ask, changed words marked inside changed lines, side by side or one column, and reviewer comments pinned to lines.

props.name: order
props.notes: `salience` lists the files with the most real change first, so a reviewer starts where it matters. Moved code does not count.

props.name: onDecideHunk
props.type: ((path: string, hunk: number, decision: HunkDecision, digest: string) => void) | undefined
props.notes: Adds accept and reject on each hunk. Each decision is tied to a digest of the file, so it stops counting once the file changes.

props.name: onView
props.type: ((path: string, viewed: boolean, digest: string) => void) | undefined
props.notes: Called when a file is marked viewed or not, with the digest of what was viewed.

FlowCanvas.doc: A diagram you can move around in: drag to pan, ctrl or cmd and scroll to zoom, a minimap, zoom controls, swimlanes when nodes have owners, rounded orthogonal edges, and a click on any node to trace what feeds it and what it leads to. The layout is computed, so you only describe the steps and how they connect.

DataGrid.doc: A data grid that holds up at thousands of rows: only the visible rows are drawn, headers and the first column stay put, columns sort (shift-click for a second sort key), filter (">100", "10..20", or text), resize and export, rows select with click and shift-click, and the keyboard works throughout.

ControlChart.doc: A control chart for a failure rate. It draws the centre line and the 1, 2 and 3 sigma limits for each point's own sample size, and marks points that break the standard run rules. A signal means "look closer", and the wording says so: it never claims something is broken, and a quiet chart never claims it is safe.

props.name: baseline
props.notes: Points used to set the centre line. Defaults to all of them.

props.name: rules
props.notes: Which run rules to apply. Defaults to the four Western Electric rules. Use `NELSON` for all eight.

props.name: markers
props.notes: Vertical markers, for example a model release. `at` is a point index.

Sankey.doc: Where cases go. Bands are sized by volume on one scale. Hover a band or a node to see exactly how much took that path, and any node where more came in than went out shows the cases that were not accounted for.

ApprovalQueue.doc: A review queue where an approval is bound to the exact plan. The plan is hashed, every decision records the hash it was made on, and a decision on an older version stops counting the moment the plan changes. Buttons say what will happen, the page says whether it can be undone and what evidence was checked, a second approval must come from a different person, and anything not decided in time expires instead of going through.

props.name: reviewer
props.notes: Who is looking. They cannot decide their own requests or decide twice.

props.name: blind
props.notes: Hide other reviewers' decisions until this reviewer has decided, so a second approval is an independent one.

props.name: onDecide
props.type: ((id: string, decision: DecisionKind, planHash: string, message?: string) => void) | undefined

props.name: onEdit
props.notes: Called with the edited plan when a reviewer saves a change to it. The plan, and so the hash every approval is bound to, is now the new one.

props.name: onSelect
props.notes: Called with the id of the request being shown, including the first one on load.

AutonomyGate.doc: When an agent has earned more autonomy. It counts how often a person agreed with what the agent proposed, puts an exact interval on it and compares the lower bound with your rule. It says "eligible", never "promoted": a person decides.

props.name: tier
props.notes: The tier the agent runs at now.

props.name: cases
props.notes: Agent proposals paired with what a person decided.

props.name: rule
props.notes: For example 90% agreement over at least 30 cases.

props.name: looks
props.notes: How many times this result has been checked. Each look widens the interval.

EvidenceTable.doc: Each extracted value with the places it was read from. Coverage and conflicts are counted from the sources. There is no confidence score: a value has a source or it does not, and two sources either agree or they do not.

props.name: documents
props.notes: Your document text by id. A source with a `docId` has its excerpt looked up in it, and one that is not there is flagged.

props.name: available
props.notes: What the source documents contain, so values the agent left out can be named.

PlanVsActual.doc: What the agent said it would do next to what it did. Skipped, failed, blocked, out-of-order and unplanned steps are found by comparing the two lists, so the agent's own account of its run never decides the result.

RunInspector.doc: One agent run, seen four ways, with the four questions people ask of a run answered first: did it finish, did it follow the plan, were the tool calls sound, and does each value have a source. Every answer is worked out from the spans, the plan and the evidence you pass in.

props.name: plan
props.notes: With `actual`, adds the plan tab.

props.name: evidence
props.notes: Adds the evidence tab.

props.name: health
props.notes: How strictly to check the trace. See `traceHealth`.

ApprovalChain.doc: Who has to approve, in order, and who is being waited on. Each step has a time limit. A decision from the person who asked, from someone who is not the named approver, or from someone who already approved an earlier step does not count, and the step says why.

props.name: requester
props.notes: Who asked. Their own decision never counts.

HandoffPacket.doc: What an agent hands a person when it stops. The packet is checked, not trusted: a handoff is complete only when a person could act without asking the agent anything, and every part that is missing is named.

props.name: handoff
props.notes: What the agent handed over. Anything missing is shown as missing, not hidden.

ApprovalWorkspace.doc: A review workspace: the queue on the left, and for the request you are looking at, who has to approve and who is late, where each value came from, and what the agent handed over. A tab only appears when the request has that part, so nothing is shown as empty.

props.name: onDecide
props.type: ((id: string, decision: import("/Users/karthik/React-projects/ai-startup/orlune/src/index").DecisionKind, planHash: string, message?: string) => void) | undefined

DeadlineGantt.doc: Every deadline clock on one time axis. A bar runs from the start to the finish (or to now, if still open), a diamond marks the deadline, and any time spent past the deadline is hatched red. Met, running, overdue, and missed-but-remedied are worked out from the dates, never passed in.

ActivityHeatmap.doc: A calendar of activity. Colour is the day's quartile among active days. A red mark means a guarantee was breached that day.

PermissionGrant.doc: What an agent is allowed to do, how much of each allowance is left and when it ends. Status comes from the grant, the clock and what has been used, so a grant the agent describes as current is still shown as expired if it is.

props.name: now
props.notes: Fixed clock for the verdicts. Defaults to the current time.

props.name: userScopes
props.notes: What each person may do. With it, a delegated grant is checked against the person it acts for.

BudgetMeter.doc: Spend against a limit for a period. The marker shows how much of the period has gone, so a bar that is further along than the marker is ahead of pace. The projection is a straight line you can check with a calculator.

props.name: samples
props.notes: Cumulative use over time. With three or more, the recent rate is fitted; with fewer, the average so far is used.

AutonomyBoard.doc: Every agent in one list: its tier, whether a person's agreement with it has earned a higher one, what its grants and budget look like, and anything that needs a look. Each row is worked out from that agent's own cases, grants and budget, and the eligible tag is a prompt for a person, not a promotion.

props.name: now
props.notes: Fixed clock for the verdicts. Defaults to the current time.

RecordViewer.doc: One record on one page: the verifier's verdict, each guarantee against what was found, the signed events and the hash chain. It renders only what the verifier returned, and shows a record as verified only when the verdict and its own details agree. The export is the verifier's output, not a new signature.

props.name: result
props.notes: What `verifyRecord` returned. Without one the viewer says "Not verified".

InputRequest.doc: A form an agent hands to a person when it needs information it does not have. Every answer is checked against the field it was asked for before it goes back, so the agent never receives a value of a kind it did not ask for.

props.name: asked
props.notes: Why the agent stopped to ask, in its own words. Shown as the agent's, not as a fact.

props.name: context
props.notes: What the person is deciding about, as label and value rows.

props.name: onSubmit
props.notes: Called with the checked values. Numbers are numbers and blank optional fields are left out.

props.name: from
props.notes: Who is asking, so the person can tell.

props.name: link
props.notes: For something that must not pass through this page, such as a password or a payment: a link the person opens instead. Only plain https links are offered, with the site named.

props.name: onDecline
props.notes: Adds a way to turn the request down. The agent should be told, so this is a callback and not a default.

props.name: onCancel
props.notes: Adds a way to close the request without answering either way.

props.name: onResult
props.notes: The answer in the shape MCP elicitation uses: accept with the values, decline, or cancel. Called alongside the callbacks above.

RunBranches.doc: One run seen as a tree of saved states. Where it was replayed from an earlier step with something changed, the tree forks, and any two ends can be set side by side: where they split, what only each did, and exactly which saved values differ at the end. Everything is read from the saved states, so nothing about the difference is guessed.

props.name: checkpoints
props.notes: Saved states of one run, each pointing at the one it came from. A run replayed from a step with something changed forks there.

props.name: defaultA
props.notes: Which two ends to compare first. Defaults to the first two.

RunVariants.doc: Many runs grouped by the path they took, the way a process-mining variant view does. Each path says how many runs took it, whether it followed the plan and what it skipped, and how often it failed with an exact interval, so a path that failed 3 of 4 times is not mistaken for one that failed 300 of 400.

props.name: plan
props.notes: The path the agent was meant to take. Without it, paths are only grouped and counted.

VerifyBadge.doc: A small mark that says whether a record checked out, and opens to the full result. It fits inside a table row or a header. It shows "Verified" only when the verifier's verdict and its own details agree, and says "Not verified" when it has no result, never a tick it was not given.
